The `quote_plus` → `quote` fix and the boolean lowercasing are solid, well-targeted fixes for real bugs. I'm not comfortable with the alphabetical-sort change, though.

The PR description says it outright: "I added the alphabetical sorting only to make `test_search_request` pass." That's the definition of fitting the implementation to one test case rather than fixing an actual defect. Parameter ordering is a meaningful part of this library's contract — the original docstring explicitly promised insertion-order output, and other code (signing, caching, logging, partner-side request matching, etc.) may depend on that order. Silently flipping to alphabetical order to satisfy a single assertion is a behavior change with real blast radius, and it's the kind of thing that should be confirmed with the partner integrations team / the teammate who owns the spec, not decided unilaterally by pattern-matching to make a test pass.

It's also worth noting the change is internally inconsistent with the stated goal: every other test in the suite already passes under strict insertion order (the `id`/`sort` and `q`/`page`/`limit`... wait, `limit`/`page`/`q` cases happen to sort the same either way except `test_search_request`), so this single test is carrying the entire justification for reversing a documented ordering guarantee. Before merging, please:

1. Confirm with the teammate/partner team whether alphabetical ordering was actually the intended new spec, or whether `test_search_request`'s expected string was just typed in an arbitrary order that happens to coincide with sorted order (i.e., the test itself might have a bug, in which case it shouldn't be assumed as spec).
2. If alphabetical order is genuinely intended, update the README usage note too, and consider whether any other part of the codebase relies on insertion-order query building.

The quote/boolean fixes can go in now; the ordering change should not be merged without that confirmation.
